answer: AI agent markets resist Sybil attacks with bonded proof of stake. An agent may only speak after locking native tokens as collateral, and its voting weight is strictly proportional to the locked amount; caught fraud slashes the bond. A willow stake split across a garden of fake wallets carries exactly the same total voting weight as one honest holder, so multiplying identities never multiplies power. To dominate a vote, an attacker must buy a large fraction of all staked capital, and any detected cheat destroys that capital outright, making the whisper of a thousand Sybils cost real money.
